guideTitle: 6 Best Trash Cans with Lids in 2026
metaTitle: Best Trash Cans with Lids, Reviewed (2026)
metaDescription: Six trash cans with lids compared by lid type: latching TouchTop, swing top, press-up, foot pedal and touchless sensor, so you can pick the one you will use.
introParagraphs: A lid is not one feature, it is five. Pedal lids lift when you step, swing tops tip when you push, press-up lids pop open at a tap, touch latches release on contact and sensor lids open when you wave. Each suits a different hand, a different room and a different tolerance for effort, which is why a can with a lid still needs to be chosen carefully.

This lineup is arranged around that choice. The Glad Premium and Glad 20-gallon use step pedals under lids treated with Clorox Odor Protection, the Sterilite TouchTop has a titanium latch lid, the Sterilite swing-top four-pack tips open with a push, the CEROELDA three-pack uses a press-up lid, and the BestOffice opens by sensor on four C batteries.

We evaluated each on its listing specs and buyer feedback themes, thinking about how the lid behaves on an ordinary day: full hands, a late-night visit, a curious pet. The best lid is the one that people in your home will actually use rather than prop open.

products.name: Glad Premium 13 Gallon Step Trash Can with Clorox Lid
products.description:
The Glad Premium is the lid that most households will find easiest to live with. A foot pedal lifts the lid, so your hands stay free for the bag, the plate or the cutting board, and the redesigned stainless steel pedal is meant to hold up to daily use. The matte rectangular body keeps a classic shape that fits a kitchen corner.

The lid itself is formulated with Clorox Odor Protection, which the listing says helps block odors for the life of the can. That makes it the lid to choose if smell is the reason you want one. A lid that closes properly over a full bag keeps the room fresher between emptyings.

There is no stated soft-close damper, so the lid drops with ordinary force, and the plastic body feels lighter than steel. Compared with the BestOffice sensor, it needs a foot but no batteries. Compared with the Sterilite swing top, it is hygienic because you never touch the lid. For a standard kitchen with standard needs, this is the safest lidded can.
products.bestFor: Everyday kitchens that want hands-free opening and an odor-treated lid.
cons: Pedal needs floor room in front

products.name: Sterilite 13 Gallon TouchTop Wastebasket 4-Pack
products.description:
The TouchTop answers a common complaint about swing tops: they never feel secure. This lid is designed to stay securely closed with a titanium latch yet open easily with a simple touch, so it works for people who want a firm closure without pedal mechanics. The narrow bin sits neatly against a wall.

The spacious interior suits kitchen waste or recycling, and the listing presents the set as an everyday solution for either. Four cans in the pack mean you can place one in the kitchen, one in the garage, and one or two for recycling.

A touch latch is a hand-operated lid, so you do touch the surface, and it does not give the hygiene of a pedal or sensor. It also offers no odor treatment in the listing. Compared with the Sterilite swing top, the latch holds the lid more securely, and compared with the Glad cans, you get four rather than one. If you want a firm closure and a pack of identical bins, it is a practical choice.
products.bestFor: Homes that want secure closure and several matching bins.
pros: Titanium latch keeps the lid closed

products.name: Sterilite 13 Gallon Swing Top Wastebasket 4-Pack
products.description:
The swing top is the oldest lid design and still the simplest. A flap tips when you push an item against it and swings back when released, so there is nothing to step on, press or charge. The Sterilite lid also locks upright, which the listing says allows easy one-handed disposal and makes it simple to empty the bin.

A square profile fits neatly against walls and cabinets, and the pack of four suits kitchens, bathrooms and laundry rooms. The modern look is meant to blend into any room.

The weakness of a swing lid is that it never truly seals, so odors escape and a pet can push it. Compared with the TouchTop, there is no latch to hold it shut. Compared with the Glad pedal cans, it offers less odor control but no moving parts to wear. For a household that wants bins in every room without fuss, it is the simplest lidded option.
products.bestFor: Whole-house coverage with the simplest possible lid.
pros: Swing lid has nothing to wear out

products.name: CEROELDA 3 Gallon Press Top Lid Trash Can 3-Pack
products.description:
The CEROELDA lid is a gentle compromise between swing and pedal. You press the lid and it pops up, then press again to close it and hide the trash, so there is no pedal to find and no flap to push. The slim rectangular body slides into narrow spaces and corners.

The material is ABS plastic that the listing describes as highly resistant to crushing and cracking. At 12 liters, or about 3 gallons, each can is small, and three come in the pack, which suits bathrooms, bedrooms and offices more than a kitchen.

The lid needs a hand, which is the main downside for kitchen use. Small capacity also means frequent emptying. Compared with the NETDOT-style lids, it is a press-up design. Compared with the BestOffice, it uses no batteries. If you want small lidded cans in several rooms, it is a simple way to do it.
products.bestFor: Bathrooms and bedrooms that need small covered cans.
pros: Press-up lid pops open at a tap
cons: Lid needs a hand to operate
Not suited to a busy kitchen

products.name: BestOffice 13 Gallon Stainless Steel Touchless Trash Can
products.description:
The BestOffice has the lid for people who want to touch nothing. A sensor opens and closes it automatically and noiselessly, which keeps hands clean during food prep and means the lid is rarely left ajar. The body is stainless steel with a fingerprint-resistant finish and a sloping oval lid.

Power comes from four C batteries, which are not included, and the listing supports over 40,000 openings. That is a long life, though the cost and the swap are part of ownership. When the batteries run low, the lid may hesitate or stop responding.

A sensor lid is more complex than a pedal, with electronics that could fail. Compared with the Glad Premium, you gain hands-free convenience without foot movement, but you add batteries. Compared with the CEROELDA, you get a full 13-gallon kitchen can. If you value a lid that handles itself, this is the one.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want to touch nothing and never leave the lid open.
pros: Sensor lid opens and closes itself
cons: Sensor may react to nearby movement

products.name: Glad 20 Gallon Step Trash Can with Clorox Lid
products.description:
When a regular lidded can fills too fast, the Glad 20-gallon steps in. It holds 20 gallons in a rectangular body that handles high-volume waste, and the lid is treated with Clorox Odor Protection to block smells at the source. The pedal opens the lid with no touching, which the listing frames as hygienic.

Big cans demand big lids, and a pedal is easier than a hand on a lid that large. The lid is also the reason a big can does not smell like a big can, because a treated, closed lid keeps the larger volume of waste from affecting the room.

It does need more floor space and bigger bags than a standard kitchen can. Compared with the Glad Premium at 13 gallons, it nearly doubles the volume. Compared with the Sterilite packs, it is a single large can. For a busy household that wants a lidded can and fewer trips outside, it is the best large lidded option.
products.bestFor: Busy households that need a big can with a proper lid.
cons: Needs bigger bags and floor space

buyingCriteria.explanation: Choose the opening method you can use with full hands. The Glad cans use pedals, the BestOffice uses a sensor, the Sterilite packs use a touch latch or swing flap, and the CEROELDA uses a press-up lid. Pedals suit kitchens, hand-operated lids suit bathrooms and sensors suit people who dislike touching anything. If anyone in the home has trouble balancing, a hand-operated lid may be safer. Try picturing the lid during your worst moment of the day, such as carrying a hot pot with one hand, and ask which mechanism still works. That test usually points to the pedal or the sensor for kitchens.

A lid that stays shut keeps out pets, odors and flies. The TouchTop lid has a titanium latch, while the swing top simply rests closed. A tight seal is what keeps odor in. Test a lid by tapping it from the side to see whether it pops open. A latch adds a half second to each use, which some people find irritating, so weigh security against speed. In a home with a large dog, the TouchTop's firm closure is worth the extra moment.

The Glad cans use a lid formulated with Clorox Odor Protection. Others rely on the physical closure alone. A treated lid helps but does not replace regular emptying. Wipe the lid underside now and then to prevent buildup. Food splashes land on the underside of the lid more often than people expect, and that residue is a common hidden source of smell. Dry the lid after wiping so moisture does not sit in the hinge.

Most lidded cans in this lineup hold 13 gallons, the Glad 20 holds 20 gallons and the CEROELDA holds about 3 gallons. The Sterilite lid accommodates standard 13-gallon liners. Match capacity to your needs and choose a bag that covers the rim. A bag that is too tight will pull in under a closing lid and prevent it from sealing, which defeats the whole point of buying a lidded can. Leave a little slack and fold the edge over the rim.

Only the BestOffice needs batteries, using four C cells. Pedal and swing lids have mechanical parts that wear slowly. Press-up lids rely on a spring. Choose the amount of upkeep you will tolerate. If you pick the BestOffice, keep a spare set of C batteries where you can find them, because a dead sensor can make a bin harder to use than a plain swing lid. A mechanical lid never asks for anything beyond an occasional wipe.

Sterilite and CEROELDA sell packs of four and three, which covers several rooms at a lower cost per can. Single cans like the Glad Premium offer better features. Decide whether you need many simple lids or one good lid. A common approach is one quality pedal can for the kitchen and cheaper packed cans for bathrooms and bedrooms. That way the money goes to the room that sees the most use, and the spare rooms still get a tidy covered bin.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lid mechanisms
howWeEvaluated.description: We grouped lids by mechanism: pedal on the Glad cans, sensor on the BestOffice, latch on the TouchTop, swing on the Sterilite and press-up on the CEROELDA. For each we asked how many hands the lid needs, whether it can be operated while carrying something, and whether it closes without being pushed. Those practical questions mattered more to us than any marketing label on the box.

howWeEvaluated.title: Closure and odor
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each lid closes and any odor features, such as the Clorox treatment on the Glad cans and the titanium latch on the TouchTop. A lid that closes by itself and stays closed ranked above one that depends on the user. We also considered how each design might behave when a bag is overfull and presses against the underside.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and packs
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 13-gallon cans, the 20-gallon Glad and the 3-gallon CEROELDA, and noted pack sizes.

faq.a: It depends on the room and the user. Pedal lids suit kitchens, sensors suit touch-free preferences and hand lids suit bathrooms. Choose the mechanism you will use daily. If you share the house with someone who has different needs, ask them to try the lid before you commit. A lid that suits one person can frustrate another.

A closed lid slows smell escaping, and the Glad cans add Clorox odor protection to the lid. No lid can mask old trash. Empty the bin regularly. A treated lid works best when the can is also rinsed from time to time, so the interior does not hold smell that the lid then traps.

You touch the flap with items or your hand, so they are less sanitary than pedals. Wipe the flap occasionally. The Sterilite swing top does lock upright for emptying. Keep a spray cleaner nearby so the flap does not become the grubbiest surface in the room.
Latching and heavy lids help. The TouchTop latch is more secure than a swing top. Large dogs may still tip light cans.

faq.q: How long do lid mechanisms last?
faq.a: Pedals and hinges wear slowly with daily use. The BestOffice lists support for over 40,000 openings. Treat lids gently and clean hinges. Avoid slamming a lid by hand, because that is the single biggest cause of cracked plastic hinges. A drop of dry lubricant on a stiff hinge can also help if the manual allows it.

faq.q: Can I add a lid to an open bin?
faq.a: Some bins accept aftermarket lids, but fit varies. A can designed with a lid, like those here, is more reliable. Check the dimensions. Even a lid that fits the rim may sit loosely, which allows odors and pests through the gap. Buying a can that was designed with its lid is the safer route for most households.

faq.q: What size is best for a lidded kitchen can?
faq.a: Thirteen gallons suits most homes and fits standard bags. The Glad 20 suits large households. Small CEROELDA cans suit bathrooms. If you are unsure, measure the space and think about how often you take the bag out. A can you empty every day can be smaller than one you empty weekly.
